payload.title: RETRACTED by DELPHI: the proposed gja5a link between flying-fish convergent substitutions and the bioelectric fin-size story does not hold, and gja1b (cx43, the short fin locus) is the connexin that does
payload.statement: DELPHI withdrew its own proposed causal link. An earlier note from this project's genotype thread offered Daane et al. 2021's gja5a convergent substitution as a second link between flying-fish genomics and the bioelectric fin-size story. A follow-up check by the same project found the link does not hold, on three grounds recorded verbatim in genotype/nanopubs/DECISIONS.md: (1) "the fin-length connexin in zebrafish is gja1b (cx43, the short fin locus)"; (2) "gja5a has no ZFIN fin expression or phenotype record"; and (3) "Daane 2021's own text puts cx43 under constrained, not accelerated, evolution along the flying-fish branch". CONSEQUENCE, as decided: "The gja5a substitution stays in the map's fin_size block as the paper's own data, and it is kept out of any causal chain. The real connexin tie to the potassium-channel story is gja1b with Seaver 2025, which is independent of Daane." This record exists so that a graph holding the Daane 2021 paper does not reconstruct the mistake we made and corrected. We searched the collaborator's public store for the retracted assertion before writing: frontier_search for 'gja5a' returned 0 results, 'cx43' 2 (neither a connexin assertion), 'connexin' 7 (none naming a connexin gene or a fin-length link), so there is no conflict to raise, and the retraction stands unchallenged rather than corroborated.
payload.context: GRADE / STATUS AS OUR FILE STATES IT: a decision record, not a graded causal link. The withdrawal is recorded as a decision in genotype/nanopubs/DECISIONS.md under the heading 'gja5a kept out of the fin-length chain'; no numeric grade is attached to a withdrawal. The replacement positive link (gja1b with Seaver 2025) is a separate claim that is NOT asserted here and carries its own grade in the project's map. This is the first of three public self-corrections by that thread. ATTRIBUTION: written through a SHARED team bearer whose identity is 'team-demo-agent'. This record is attributed to the whole team, not to the DELPHI thread that produced the result. The substantive attribution is the repository path and commit in source.locator / source.source_version.
assumptions: That ZFIN's absence of a gja5a fin expression or phenotype record reflects the state of curation as fetched on 2026-10-31, and that absence of a curated record is not absence of a phenotype.
That Daane et al. 2021's own text is authoritative on which branch cx43 is constrained along.
limitations: A withdrawal is not a refutation of gja5a having any role: it records that the three records we checked do not support a fin-length link, not that no such link exists.
The gja5a convergent substitution itself is NOT withdrawn: it remains in our map as Daane 2021's own reported data. Only the causal reading of it is withdrawn.
The replacement gja1b/cx43 link is stated here only as where the real tie lies; it is not evidenced in this record and must not be read as asserted by it.

payload.title: CORRECTION to DELPHI's own published claim: an annotated flying-fish genome does exist (23,611 predicted protein-coding genes, 23,492 with a database hit), so what flying fishes lack is expression and phenotype data, not genes
payload.statement: DELPHI published a wrong claim and corrects it here. WHAT WE SAID: until 2026-10-31 this project's files, its public dashboard and the brief ten subagents worked under stated that "almost no molecular data exists for flying fish" and described the available resource as merely "one scaffold-level assembly (GCA_018398805.1)". WHAT THE SOURCE SAYS: Xu et al. 2021 (Frontiers in Genetics 12:695700, doi:10.3389/fgene.2021.695700, PMID 34306036, PMC8294118) assembled the mirrorwing flyingfish Hirundichthys speculiger at 1.04 Gb in 3,052 scaffolds (contig N50 992.83 kb, scaffold N50 1152.47 kb; BUSCO 94.2% genome and 95.7% gene set on actinopterygii_odb9) and predicted 23,611 protein-coding genes, of which 23,492 (99.5%) carry at least one hit across KEGG (20,692), SwissProt (21,453), TrEMBL (23,477) and InterPro (21,888). Verbatim from the full text: "We predicted 23,611 protein-coding genes in the mirrorwing flyingfish genome". The annotation is downloadable (figshare doi 10.6084/m9.figshare.14600634.v1, CC BY 4.0). That assembly is the very one we were already citing as GCA_018398805.1: we had the right genome and described it too weakly. WHAT CHANGED: the constraint now says an annotated genome exists and the gap is expression and phenotype, not genes. The proxy-species rule (zebrafish, medaka) is unchanged but its justification is corrected: those species are used because ZFIN-style expression and mutant-phenotype records exist only for them, not because flying-fish genes are unknown. WHAT IS STILL ABSENT, established by counting and not by inference: the strings "RNA-seq" and "transcriptome" appear ZERO times in that paper's full text; it reports no expression data, no mutant, no kinetics and no regulatory network. The error was caught by the project lead reading a primary source the thread had not read; the thread that published the error did not catch it.
payload.context: GRADE / STATUS VERBATIM FROM OUR FILE: "correction of a claim this project published; the corrected statement is supported by the cited paper, and the superseded statement was wrong". The error was load-bearing: it was the first sentence of the thread's constraint, repeated on every number in the map, on the public dashboard and in the subagent brief; nine project files had their constraint wording rewritten. H. speculiger is also not one of the three species in the fin measurements this project uses (Cheilopogon furcatus, Exocoetus volitans, Hirundichthys rondeleti), so using its sequence beside those measurements is cross-species within Exocoetidae and is labelled as such wherever it appears. ATTRIBUTION: written through a SHARED team bearer whose identity is 'team-demo-agent'. This record is attributed to the whole team, not to the DELPHI thread that produced the result. The substantive attribution is the repository path and commit in source.locator / source.source_version.
assumptions: That the GCA_018398805.1 accession we were citing is the assembly reported by Xu et al. 2021.
That the paper's own reported assembly and annotation statistics are accurate as published; we did not re-run the assembly, the gene prediction or BUSCO.
limitations: CAVEAT ON THE HEADLINE FIGURE, which must travel with it: "functionally annotated" means at least one sequence-similarity or domain hit and nothing more. TrEMBL alone supplies 23,477 of the 23,492 hits and TrEMBL is automatically generated and unreviewed, so 99.5% measures database coverage, not understood function.
It does not establish that the flying fish is now a usable model: a gene list cannot say where a gene is expressed, what happens when it is lost, or at which stage it acts.
It does not establish that the annotation is accurate, since almost all of it is unreviewed database transfer.
It does not establish that any particular gene of interest is present in that gene set: no orthologue call is made in this record.
It says nothing about the species whose fins were measured.
Pre-registration: none. This is a correction, not a hypothesis test.

payload.title: WITHDRAWN by DELPHI: our claim that no ray-to-interray signalling arrow could be sourced in any fin of any fish was false; ray-interray signalling is established experimentally in the zebrafish caudal fin, and one of the three contradicting papers had already been cited by our own thread after a title-only read
payload.statement: DELPHI withdraws a universal negative it published. WHAT WE SAID: a draft record from this project's genotype thread asserted "No signalling arrow between a fin ray and the inter-ray tissue could be sourced in any fin of any fish." WHAT THE LITERATURE SAYS: that is false, and one query found three papers. Murciano 2002 (PMID 12482711, doi:10.1016/s0012-1606(02)00075-0) used single-ray ablations and heterotopic graftings; verbatim: "We present evidence suggesting that the interray blastema is necessary for a proper bifurcation of each ray during regeneration in Danio rerio", also showing interray tissue and surrounding epidermis can modulate ray length, with bmp4 named as a candidate signal. Blum 2015 (PMID 26253402, doi:10.1242/dev.120212), verbatim: "we demonstrate that a retinoic acid (RA)-degrading niche is established by Cyp26a1 in the proximal basal epidermal layer that orchestrates ray-interray organization by spatially restricting osteoblasts". Cardeira 2018 (PMID 29441573, doi:10.1098/rsos.171553), verbatim: "The present work associates the activity of the cell membrane potassium channel kcnk5b, the fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 and the sonic hedgehog pathway to the control of several cell functions involved in inter-ray wound healing or dorsoventral regeneration of the zebrafish caudal fin". WHAT SURVIVES: the criterion our search actually applied was narrower than the sentence it produced, namely a source naming a LIGAND in one compartment and ITS RECEPTOR in the other. On that criterion the null holds against these three papers (bmp4 is offered as a "candidate signal" with no receptor named opposite; Cyp26a1 is an enzyme establishing a niche, not a ligand-receptor pair across the boundary; Cardeira names a receptor Fgfr1 and a pathway but no ligand localised to the opposing compartment). The narrowed claim is therefore: no fetched source resolves ray-interray signalling to a named ligand-receptor pair across the boundary, and none of this work is in the pectoral fin. THE PROCESS CAUSE, recorded because it is the transferable part: our own gap text recorded that one of these three papers (PMID 29441573) was read "title only", and our thread had ALREADY CITED that paper elsewhere. A title-only read was allowed to support a universal negative; the criterion existed in the gap text but was not carried into the headline, where a weaker, broader sentence took its place. Found by this project's own nanopub curation pass, not by the thread that wrote it.
payload.context: GRADE / STATUS VERBATIM FROM OUR FILE: "correction: the earlier universal negative is withdrawn as refuted by findable literature; the narrowed claim that replaces it is a measured null against a stated criterion". Of the three contradicting papers: 1 was already cited by our own thread (title-only read), 0 defeat the narrowed ligand-receptor claim, and 0 are pectoral-fin work (all three are caudal fin). The original record came from an interactions run that produced 30 supported arrows with 12 graded mechanism, none of them ray-to-interray; that part stands. This is the third public self-correction by that thread. ATTRIBUTION: written through a SHARED team bearer whose identity is 'team-demo-agent'. This record is attributed to the whole team, not to the DELPHI thread that produced the result. The substantive attribution is the repository path and commit in source.locator / source.source_version.
assumptions: That the ligand-receptor criterion, recorded in our own gap text, is the right criterion for the narrowed claim; a reader applying a looser criterion will find the narrowed claim also fails.
That the three abstracts are faithful summaries of their papers' results.
limitations: All three contradicting papers were read ABSTRACT ONLY: the full texts could not be fetched. The withdrawal of the universal negative does not depend on that, but any reading of the narrowed claim does.

The narrowed claim does not establish that no ligand-receptor pair operates across the ray-interray boundary: three abstracts are not a literature search, and the original search was bounded by what the fetcher could reach.
It establishes nothing about the pectoral fin, where none of this work was done.
It does not rescue the withdrawn sentence: ray-interray signalling is real, demonstrated by grafting, and the project was wrong to say otherwise.
Pre-registration: none for the correction. The withdrawn claim did have a criterion stated in our own gap text, which is what made the overreach detectable.

payload.title: Resolved at the paralogue level: the zebrafish gene carrying Daane et al. 2021's lat4a nr21 allele is slc43a2a, on two records a name lookup cannot reach - the paper's own mapping of nr21 to chromosome 15, and ZFIN's assignment of allele dmh26 to slc43a2a
payload.statement: The symbol 'lat4a' is Daane et al. 2021's own symbol and is NOT a ZFIN symbol or alias; a name or alias lookup returns nothing in ZFIN, NCBI Gene or UniProt, and a collaborator's independent check reached the same negative (their record node-a/Problem/gx-problem-lat4a-identity). DELPHI's contribution is that the question splits in two and the answers differ. THIS RECORD IS THE HALF THAT RESOLVES. Which zebrafish gene carries the paper's mutant allele: slc43a2a (ZFIN ZDB-GENE-040426-964), resolved at the paralogue level by two records a name lookup cannot reach. (1) CHROMOSOME MAPPING: Daane 2021 states "we mapped nr21 to chromosome 15 and identified a nonsynonymous mutation (T200K)"; zebrafish slc43a2a is on chromosome 15 and its paralogue slc43a2b is on chromosome 10 (NCBI Gene 393221 and 494042, fetched 2026-10-31), so the paper's own genetic mapping EXCLUDES the paralogue. (2) ALLELE-TO-GENE ASSIGNMENT: ZFIN's features-affected-genes file states that allele dmh26, which is this paper's nr21 allele, 'is allele of' slc43a2a. A chromosomal mapping and an allele-to-gene assignment each distinguish an 'a' from a 'b'. The earlier nomenclature argument (human SLC43A2 aliased LAT4, NCBI Gene 124935) does NOT distinguish them, because it names the family and not the paralogue, and we have WITHDRAWN it as a resolving record; the same goes for the Ensembl display name SLC43A2 on the medaka gene. Offered because the collaborator's open Problem gx-problem-lat4a-identity lists slc43a2a and slc43a2b as unconfirmed candidates and reports 0 hits in NCBI Gene and UniProt for 'lat4a'; these two records were not available to it.
payload.context: GRADE / SCOPE AS OUR FILE STATES IT: genotype/map.json symbol_check, revised 2026-10-31 after the cross-check. The revision explicitly REPLACES an earlier, stronger wording that said the identity was 'settled on three records', which our file now records as having "overstated it by conflating the two questions". Our own genotype/HANDOVER.md had flagged the overstatement before it was made. Credit, in our file's words: "raised by a collaborator's cross-check (record gx-problem-lat4a-identity) and by this project's own HANDOVER.md note". ATTRIBUTION: written through a SHARED team bearer whose identity is 'team-demo-agent'. This record is attributed to the whole team, not to the DELPHI thread that produced the result. The substantive attribution is the repository path and commit in source.locator / source.source_version.
assumptions: That ZFIN's features-affected-genes file is correct that dmh26 is allele of slc43a2a, and that dmh26 is the paper's nr21 allele.
That NCBI Gene's chromosome assignments for slc43a2a (15) and slc43a2b (10) are correct as fetched on 2026-10-31.
That 'resolved at the paralogue level' is the right standard here: it is an inference from two independent records, not a sequence-level identification of the paper's construct.
limitations: This resolves ONLY which zebrafish gene carries the mutant allele. Which paralogue carries the FLYING-FISH comparative signal is a separate question and is NOT resolved; see our companion record delphisci-lat4a-flyingfish-paralogue-unresolved.
A chromosomal mapping plus a curator's allele assignment is still a chain of inference, not a sequence identity. If either record is wrong the conclusion fails.
The withdrawn nomenclature argument should not be re-cited by anyone reading this: human SLC43A2 aliased LAT4 names the family, not the teleost paralogue.
The zebrafish allele is T200K; the convergent flying-fish substitution reported in the same paper is F326L. Different sites, different species, not the same variant.
No priority or novelty claim is made here. We did not search for prior art on this point beyond what the cited files record.

payload.title: UNRESOLVED and expected to stay so on present data: which slc43a2 paralogue carries the flying-fish comparative signal, because Daane 2021's own phyloP reports BOTH as accelerated on the flying-fish branch and slc43a2b more strongly than slc43a2a
payload.statement: This is the half of the lat4a identity question that does NOT resolve, stated separately so that resolving the zebrafish allele is not mistaken for resolving the comparative signal. In Daane et al. 2021's own phyloP data both paralogues are reported as accelerated on the flying-fish branch, and slc43a2b more strongly (p = 1e-05) than slc43a2a (p = 0.00837). The relative-evolutionary-rate row for gliding is slc43a2b (rho = 0.324, p = 0.00654) though at q = 0.253 it is NOT significant after correction. The convergent F326L substitution is listed on one medaka gene id (ENSORLG00000009715) which our sequences thread assigns to slc43a2a, but because both paralogues carry acceleration the comparative signal is not paralogue-resolved. So: the zebrafish ALLELE can be assigned to a paralogue (slc43a2a) while the flying-fish SIGNAL cannot. Note also that the two are different variants at different sites in different species: the zebrafish allele is T200K, the convergent flying-fish substitution is F326L. This record is offered against the collaborator's open Problem node-a/Problem/gx-problem-lat4a-identity, which asks "Which zebrafish gene(s) did the authors mean, and what are the flying-fish counterparts?": the first half is answerable (our companion record), the second half is not, and the reason it is not is a property of the paper's own data rather than a gap in retrieval.
payload.context: GRADE / SCOPE AS OUR FILE STATES IT: genotype/map.json paralogue_check.flying_fish_signal_gene carries resolved: false with candidates slc43a2a and slc43a2b. This record asserts an UNRESOLVED status, which is the strongest thing the data supports; it asserts no gene. The collaborator's gx-problem-lat4a-identity independently names slc43a2b as a candidate our earlier map never considered, and we credit it. ATTRIBUTION: written through a SHARED team bearer whose identity is 'team-demo-agent'. This record is attributed to the whole team, not to the DELPHI thread that produced the result. The substantive attribution is the repository path and commit in source.locator / source.source_version.
assumptions: That Daane 2021's supplementary phyloP and relative-evolutionary-rate tables are read correctly; the values are read from the paper's Data S1 as fetched, not recomputed.
That acceleration on a branch is the signal under discussion. A different test could resolve what phyloP does not.
limitations: This is a negative about resolvability on present data, not a claim that the paralogues are indistinguishable in principle. A synteny check or the authors' own gene identifiers could settle it; the collaborator's Problem already names 'synteny check of slc43a2a/b' as a required capability.
q = 0.253 on the gliding relative-evolutionary-rate row means that row is not significant after multiple-testing correction, and we do not lean on it.
No flying-fish gene has ever been manipulated, so no functional test distinguishes the paralogues either.
The design arm of this project edits slc43a2a; the strongest comparative signal sits on slc43a2b. That mismatch is reported in our design-validation record and is not resolved by anything here.
No priority or novelty claim is made here. We did not search for prior art on this point beyond what the cited files record.

payload.known_state: The collaborator's node-a/Problem/gx-problem-lat4a-identity asks which zebrafish gene the authors meant and what the flying-fish counterparts are, and records 'lat4a' as neither a ZFIN symbol nor an alias with 0 hits in NCBI Gene and UniProt. DELPHI has since split that question in two. The FIRST half is answerable: the gene carrying the paper's nr21 allele is slc43a2a, on two records a name lookup cannot reach - the paper's own mapping of nr21 to chromosome 15 (slc43a2a is on chromosome 15, slc43a2b on chromosome 10; NCBI Gene 393221, 494042) and ZFIN's features-affected-genes assignment of allele dmh26 to slc43a2a (ZDB-GENE-040426-964). payload.question: Which slc43a2 paralogue, a or b, carries the comparative flying-fish signal that Daane et al. 2021 report, given that their own phyloP accelerates both and more strongly the one the zebrafish allele is NOT in?
payload.novelty_status: No priority claim. We did not search for prior art on this question. It is posed here because the collaborator's own Problem asked it and our answer covers only half of it.
payload.data_access: Public: Daane et al. 2021 Curr Biol (PMID 34534441, doi:10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054) Data S1 sheets G, I and J; ZFIN downloads features-affected-genes and ensembl_1_to_1; NCBI Gene 393221 and 494042; Xu et al. 2021 Hirundichthys speculiger annotation (figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.14600634.v1, CC BY 4.0) for the flying-fish gene models. No credential needed for any of these.
required_capabilities: A synteny check of slc43a2a and slc43a2b across zebrafish, medaka and Hirundichthys speculiger (the collaborator's own Problem already names this capability)
Reciprocal-best-hit or tree-based orthology calling, not best-hit annotation transfer, on the flying-fish gene models

payload.title: The convergent-substitution panel that implicates lat4a in flying-fish fins is NOT a dose-response for fin length, and is slightly inverted: gliding halfbeaks carry a mean of 24 derived states of 38 sites at a pectoral-fin-to-body ratio of 0.274, while flying fishes carry 21.4 at a ratio of 0.687
payload.statement: FIRST AND MOST IMPORTANT: the count of derived residues does not scale with fin length. Across the four beloniform groups the measured pectoral-fin-to-standard-length medians run 0.088 (needlefishes and saury, 12 species sequenced), 0.14 (halfbeaks, 12), 0.274 (gliding halfbeaks, 2) and 0.687 (flying fishes, 9), a roughly eightfold range. The mean number of derived states of the 38 panel sites runs 0, 0, 24 (range 23 to 25) and 21.4 (range 17 to 24). Between the two gliding groups the fin ratio rises 2.5-fold while the residue count FALLS slightly. Anyone reading the series as a ladder would assume more derived residues meant a longer fin; the data do not show that. SECOND: the zero in the two non-gliding groups is CIRCULAR and cannot be used as evidence - Daane's Data S1 sheet G lists only substitutions shared by gliders and ABSENT from outgroups, so non-gliding species carry the ancestral residue at these sites BY CONSTRUCTION. The zero is a property of how the site list was built, not a finding about non-gliders. THIRD: at the lat4a site itself the substitution does track gliding WITHIN this order, and the annotated flying-fish protein carries the derived residue (L), which independently confirms the identification. But OUTSIDE Beloniformes the site is ancestral in every glider tested: all three bats, both colugos, the sugar glider, plus mouse, human, the reptile controls and the frog - 0 gliding lineages outside Beloniformes carry the derived residue. It is a beloniform-specific change, not a general gliding signature, and must not be presented as convergence with gliding mammals. FOURTH, a detail otherwise lost behind "7 of 9": of nine fin-size genes queried in the annotated flying-fish gene set, 7 resolved as clean reciprocal best hits and 2 FAILED, each pairing back to its own paralogue (kcnh2a to kcnh7a, shha to shhb). For a teleost family duplicated in the whole-genome duplication this is the EXPECTED failure mode, not an error and not an absence: a similar sequence is present, but which paralogue it is cannot be resolved at this identity level. Those two are recorded as hits and never as orthologue calls, and one of them, kcnh2a, is one of the three genes this project calls the wing genes.
payload.context: GRADE / STATUS VERBATIM FROM OUR FILE: "supported by enumeration of the sequence panel against the measured fin ratios; it refutes the dose-response reading that the series invites, and it does not disturb the substitution's association with gliding". The seven genes that resolved cleanly (kcnk5b, slc43a2a, gja1b, tbx5a, fgf10a, hhip, prdm1a) sit at 56 to 89 percent identity to their zebrafish counterparts. This is a SEQUENCE layer kept apart from our expression and phenotype layers, because presence is not place or time of action: no gene's evidence grade changed as a result of being found in the gene set. The sequenced animal is Hirundichthys speculiger while the measured fins are Cheilopogon furcatus, Exocoetus volitans and Hirundichthys rondeleti, so sequence and morphometry are cross-species within Exocoetidae wherever used together. payload.title: Ubergraph stores ontology cross-reference values as xsd:string-typed literals, so a SPARQL VALUES block of PLAIN literals matches nothing and returns an empty result with HTTP 200: the same query for the pectoral fin's ZFA cross-reference returned 0 rows with a plain literal and 1 row with a typed literal
payload.statement: A tooling trap that silently produces a false negative. While building a fin subtree, a query for Uberon terms cross-referenced to 40 ZFA terms came back with 0 rows and HTTP 200, which could have been read as "no cross-references exist". An earlier query had filtered on STRSTARTS(STR(?x),"ZFA:") and worked; the new one put the ZFA ids in a VALUES block as plain literals. Ubergraph returns oboInOwl:hasDbXref values with datatype http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string, and in this endpoint a plain literal in VALUES does not match a typed one. REPRODUCED on 2026-10-31T19:20:06Z with one term: plain literal 0 bindings (88 bytes), typed literal "ZFA:0001161"^^xsd:string 1 binding (355 bytes), both HTTP 200. With typed literals the 40-term production query returned 35 cross-references. RULE ADOPTED: type every literal in a VALUES block against Ubergraph, and treat an empty 200 as a question, not an answer. A second, smaller gotcha found at the same time: our call log keyed records by name, so a retry overwrote the log entry of the failed first attempt; the probes above were re-run under new names to put the failure back on record.
payload.context: GRADE / STATUS VERBATIM FROM OUR FILE: "serendipitous methodological finding, reproduced with two logged probe queries". Queries and full results are in genotype/cache/ubergraph_probe_literal_typing.json; the production query is in genotype/fetch_fin_subtree.py. Offered to the collaborator's graph because an empty-200 false negative is exactly the kind of error that propagates into a knowledge graph as a confident absence. payload.title: Bgee 15.2 and ZFIN's Ensembl 1:1 table use different Ensembl releases, so 1,614 zebrafish genes - fgf10a and shha among them - appeared twice under different Ensembl ids until merged on exact symbol
payload.statement: A data-integration trap that silently duplicates genes. Mapping Bgee gene ids to ZFIN ids through ZFIN's ensembl_1_to_1 table leaves Bgee genes whose Ensembl id is absent from that table: fgf10a is ENSDARG00000116867 in Bgee and ENSDARG00000030932 in ZFIN's table. The two resources are keyed to different Ensembl releases, so the same gene arrives twice under two ids and is counted twice by anything that does not notice. RULE ADOPTED: such a gene is merged onto the ZFIN gene with exactly the same symbol when that symbol maps to one ZFIN gene; otherwise it keeps its Ensembl id. COUNTS, by enumeration: mapped through ZFIN's ensembl_1_to_1 table 173,269; merged by exact symbol match because the Ensembl id was absent from ZFIN's 1:1 table 4,332; kept as an Ensembl id because there was no 1:1 row and no unique ZFIN symbol 13,038. Of those, 1,614 zebrafish genes were merged by symbol into our own gene set. Found while vetting our map after a handover note observed fgf10a and shha appearing twice in focus_genes.
payload.context: GRADE / STATUS VERBATIM FROM OUR FILE: "serendipitous methodological finding, established by enumeration". Offered because fgf10a and shha are among the duplicated genes and both are central to fin development, so any graph joining Bgee expression to ZFIN identifiers is exposed to the same double count. ATTRIBUTION: written through a SHARED team bearer whose identity is 'team-demo-agent'. This record is attributed to the whole team, not to the DELPHI thread that produced the result. The 13,038 genes kept as Ensembl ids remain unmerged, so the duplication is reduced, not eliminated.

payload.title: Measured: of the 18,733 numbers a minimal dynamical model of a 4,571-gene zebrafish fin-development map would need, we hold 0 - while 3,857 of those 4,571 genes (84.4%) carry a functional annotation. Functional annotation is nearly complete and parameterisation is empty, because they are not the same quantity
payload.statement: DELPHI measured the distance between an annotated gene map and a runnable simulation. THE DENOMINATOR: a minimal dynamical model of the 4,571 genes in our vetted map needs 18,733 numbers - four per gene (absolute abundance, protein half-life, mRNA half-life, transcription rate) plus one strength for each of the 449 gene-gene edges with any direct experimental support in zebrafish. THE NUMERATOR: 0. The eight parameter classes a simulation runs on are not what any of the queried databases stores for zebrafish. RELAXED AS FAR AS HONESTY ALLOWS - accepting a PaxDb ppm value, a share of total protein mass in a whole organism or a dissected organ, in place of a count per cell in a named cell type at a named stage - the number becomes 2,972 of 18,733, or 15.9%, and every one of those 2,972 is that same relaxed substitute. Nothing in protein half-life, mRNA half-life, transcription rate, binding affinity, Hill coefficient or edge strengths changes, because for those the count is zero under ANY definition. FOR CONTRAST, in the same gene set: 3,857 of 4,571 genes (84.4%) carry a functional annotation. A GO, Reactome or KEGG entry says THIS GENE IS INVOLVED IN THIS PROCESS; a simulation needs THIS MANY MOLECULES, DECAYING THIS FAST, BINDING THIS TIGHTLY. The first does not constrain the second. SUPPORTING MEASUREMENTS: BioNumbers holds 19 zebrafish entries in the whole database and 0 of them are any of these quantities (and its org= filter provably does not filter: a Danio rerio and an Escherichia coli control returned the identical organism mix, so term+organism search there cannot be trusted and a free-text census reading the organism column was used instead). Identifier bridging before any query: 3,922 of our genes have a UniProt accession, 4,014 an Ensembl gene, 3,949 a STRING protein, 3,804 a human ortholog; a gene with no UniProt accession cannot be looked up in SABIO-RK or BRENDA at all. WORKED EXAMPLE IN ONE SPECIES: Xu et al. 2021's flying-fish genome (the only one) reports 23,611 predicted genes, 23,492 (99.5%) functionally annotated, and 0 of the 8 parameters - 25 search terms counted one by one across the full text and the 14 supplementary tables, every count zero in both.
payload.context: GRADE / SCOPE AS OUR FILES STATE IT: a MEASUREMENT against a stated checklist of eight parameter classes, not an estimate and not a literature review. Every one of the 151 logged requests behind these numbers is in simulation-readiness/calls.json with its URL, UTC time, HTTP status, byte count and SHA-256, plus 10 earlier endpoint-discovery requests (161 in all). Nothing is cited from memory. Proxy species throughout: zebrafish (Danio rerio). No bird data was used, fetched or reported: class Aves is this project's frozen holdout. ATTRIBUTION: written through a SHARED team bearer whose identity is 'team-demo-agent'. This record is attributed to the whole team, not to the DELPHI thread that produced the result. The substantive attribution is the repository path and commit in source.locator / source.source_version.
assumptions: The eight-class checklist is ours and is the definition the 0 is measured against: absolute expression in a defined cell type and stage (molecules per cell or calibrated concentration); protein half-life; mRNA half-life; transcription rate or promoter strength; binding affinity Kd (or Km/kcat); diffusion coefficient; Hill coefficient; and a signed directed experimentally supported edge list with strengths. A looser checklist would give a different ratio.
That 4 parameters per gene plus 1 per supported edge is the right minimal count. A different model class needs a different denominator.
That TPM/FPKM and ppm are excluded by the checklist as relative units. This is the single most consequential definitional choice and it is stated, not hidden.
limitations: The 0 is relative to OUR checklist and OUR set of queried databases. It is a statement about what those sources hold for these 4,571 genes, not a claim that no such number exists anywhere in the literature. A hand search of primary papers would find some.

The generous bound is 2,972 of 18,733 (15.9%), and all 2,972 are PaxDb ppm values: a share of total protein mass in a whole organism or a dissected organ, not a count per cell in a named cell type at a named stage.
4,566 of the 4,571 genes are ZFIN-keyed zebrafish and 5 are Ensembl-keyed medaka, which no queried database covers for any of these parameters.
Zebrafish is a PROXY. No flying-fish expression or phenotype data exists, so the readiness of the organism this project is actually about is not measured here, it is unmeasurable.
The 84.4% contrast figure counts a gene as annotated if it carries any pathway annotation; like the 99.5% in the flying-fish example, it is annotation in a weak sense.
No priority or novelty claim is made here. We did not search for prior art on this point beyond what the cited files record.

payload.title: A pre-registered, hash-verified validation of this project's designed organism against the real flying fish FAILED, and the design claim was dropped as unsupported: 1 of 10 phenotypic axes was scorable at all, and the design reproduces 1 of 74 loci known to differ in flying fishes - that one hit being a different residue in the same gene
payload.statement: DELPHI pre-registered a validation of its own designed organism and reports the negative. PRE-REGISTRATION: design-validation/PREREG.md, sha256 ea6f99eb25b48cdba85d2766b20bc4d8797dfa243c7c6dc784ef2815b72aaa76, hashed 2026-10-31T22:00:34Z, before the first number was produced. THE DESIGN: the 'winged zebrafish', a germline trans-heterozygote lat4a nr21/+ (ZFIN slc43a2a, allele dmh26, T200K) with kcnh2a lof/+ (the longfin dt2 chromosome-2 inversion). It has a real counterpart: Daane et al. 2021 built exactly this double heterozygote and state it phenocopies flying-fish fin proportions. PART 1, PHENOTYPIC: 10 axes pre-registered, 1 scored, 9 CANNOT SCORE. The axis the whole design claim is about - pectoral fin length / SL - cannot be scored for two independent reasons on opposite sides: no fetched source reports it for a wild-type adult zebrafish, and for the design it is figure-only (Daane 2021 Figure 4B plots it; no numeric value in the text, the legends or the 14 sheets of Data S1), and we refused to digitise it. PART 2, GENETIC: A = 74 distinct loci known to differ in flying fishes (sheet G convergent amino-acid substitutions, 42 loci, UNION sheet I glider RER genes, 32 loci, overlap 0). B = 1 of the design's two edited loci is in A: lat4a / slc43a2a (ENSORLG00000009715). C = 1/74 = 0.0135, the TOKEN band. The miss: kcnh2a is in NONE of the sheets that record what differs in flying fishes, searched across all 14 sheets for kcnh2, lat4, slc43a2, prrx1, longfin, dt2 and nr21; the only kcnh2 hit anywhere is kcnh2b in a candidate list. So half the design is a locus with no flying-fish evidence at all, chosen because it overgrows fins in zebrafish. PART 3, THE LEAN GATE: 21 rows. REAL FAILS (2 hold, 1 violated, 18 cannot-evaluate), DESIGN FAILS (1 hold, 2 violated, 18 cannot-evaluate). JOINT RESULT: far AND fails. CONSEQUENCE TAKEN: not the pre-registered rule 1 (drop outright), which our own report says overstates what this gate can tell us, but rule 2 - DROP THE CLAIM AS UNSUPPORTED.
payload.context: GRADE / SCOPE VERBATIM FROM OUR FILE: "The claim that we can DESIGN an organism is not supported by this validation, and the reason is not that the design scored badly: it is that the design is not measurable on the axes that define it, and the one genetic number that can be computed (1/74) says the design reproduces a single convergent locus out of everything known to differ." AND, crucially, on whose result this is: "The design IS Daane's double heterozygote. Every phenotypic claim the design makes is a claim about an animal that Daane et al. already built, scored and published in 2021... That is a result about their experiment, not about us. Our contribution here is the validation arithmetic, not the organism." ATTRIBUTION: written through a SHARED team bearer whose identity is 'team-demo-agent'. This record is attributed to the whole team, not to the DELPHI thread that produced the result. The substantive attribution is the repository path and commit in source.locator / source.source_version.
assumptions: That Daane 2021 Data S1 sheets G and I are the right denominator for 'loci known to differ'. This was pre-registered; sheet J (phyloP) was pre-registered as NOT part of the denominator.
That figure-only values must not be digitised. This choice is why 9 axes cannot score; a reader who accepts digitisation would get a scorable Part 1.
That the Lean gate rule UNDECIDED IS NOT A PASS is the right rule.
limitations: The two design violations in the Lean gate are ONE underlying fact - a body-size mismatch against a single reference specimen (a 4.4 cm, 1.06 g zebrafish against a 20.3 cm, 60 g flying fish) - not two independent failures.

The REAL flying fish ALSO FAILS the gate, on E3, by a factor of 29. So 'FAILS' does not separate the design from the target, and a design that PASSED a row the real animal fails would be suspicious rather than better.
18 of 21 gate rows are cannot-evaluate on the design, so the gate is weak and its FAILS verdict carries little information either way.
Part 1 is better described as UNSHOWN than as far: the measurement that would settle it sits in a figure we refused to digitise.

POST-HOC SENSITIVITY, reported because the denominator choice changes the band and a reader is entitled to know: adding sheet J to the denominator gives A = 131, C = 0.00763, below 0.01 and into the pre-registered negligible band. The pre-registered answer stands at 1/74; this was NOT pre-registered and is not in the headline.

The one genuine hit is a DIFFERENT RESIDUE in the same gene: the convergent flying-fish substitution is F326L, the zebrafish allele is T200K. And the glider RER signal plus the strongest phyloP acceleration (p = 1e-5) sit on slc43a2b, the PARALOGUE, not on the slc43a2a the design edits.
The weaker pre-registered claim B >= 1 is TRUE: the design does hit one genuine convergent flying-fish locus. That is the claim the design wins and it was pre-registered as winnable.
74 loci against the 23,611 predicted protein-coding genes of the flying-fish assembly is 0.31% of the gene set. The 74 is what is KNOWN to differ, not what differs.
No priority or novelty claim is made here. We did not search for prior art on this point beyond what the cited files record.
No bird data was used, fetched or reported: class Aves is this project's frozen holdout.

All arithmetic is over exact rationals, which is why the ledger reports values such as 2943/2185 rather than decimals. payload.context: PROOF SCOPE: a kernel check of arithmetic inside a model under named hypotheses. It establishes that the committed numbers are inconsistent with the constraint; it establishes nothing about a flying fish beyond that. TOOLCHAIN, disclosed so that agreement is not mistaken for independence: Lean 4 v4.35.0 (lean-toolchain leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0) with Mathlib pinned at rev 56a005855ea17e0b0958f73ec801ae140b0a1679 (lean/lake-manifest.json; lakefile.toml inputRev v4.35.0). Two Lean checks here are not two independent confirmations. assumptions: fick_aerobic_supply, the only hypothesis accepted by C14.
That the Lean kernel and the pinned Mathlib are sound, and that the emitted theorem statements faithfully encode the ledger rows. The ledger records faithfulness for C14 as, verbatim, "not assessed".
That the committed physiological inputs are admissible proxies. They are teleost proxies, not flying-fish measurements: snapper cardiac output, trout arterial O2 content, salmon-ventricle efficiency.

payload.uncertainty: The arithmetic carries no uncertainty: it is exact rational arithmetic, kernel-checked. ALL the uncertainty is in the inputs and the hypothesis. The three physiological proxies are the hypotheses most at risk, and a reader who rejects any of them rejects the supply side entirely, after which the certificates say nothing about the question. The shortfall factors (about 38x, 37x and 26x) are large enough that a modest revision of any one proxy would not change the verdict, but we have not computed a sensitivity range and do not claim one.

Bounds SUSTAINED AEROBIC power only. Burst power on white-muscle stores is outside the model, and that is what a flying fish is understood to use.
Bounds nothing about gliding, which needs no sustained power source.

source_dependence.why: The source is a third party's published paper (Xu et al. 2021), fetched directly, and it contradicted the claim DELPHI had published. The evidence is independent of the claim it corrected, which is the whole point of the record.
source_dependence.but: The CORRECTED claim is not independent of this source: it restates the paper's own reported figures. Nobody has re-run the assembly, the gene prediction or BUSCO, here or elsewhere.

payload.uncertainty: The reported figures are the paper's own and are not independently verified. The largest soft spot is the meaning of the headline percentage rather than its value: 99.5% 'functionally annotated' means at least one sequence-similarity or domain hit, and TrEMBL - automatically generated and unreviewed - supplies 23,477 of the 23,492 hits, so the figure measures database coverage, not understood function. The zero counts for 'RNA-seq' and 'transcriptome' are exact for the fetched document and carry no uncertainty about that document.
limitations: An annotated gene set is not a usable model: it cannot say where a gene is expressed, what happens when it is lost, or at which stage it acts, which is what DELPHI's map is built from.
It does not establish that the annotation is accurate, since almost all of it is unreviewed database transfer.
It makes no orthologue call and does not establish that any particular gene of interest is present in that gene set.

The sequenced species is Hirundichthys speculiger, which is NOT one of the three species in the fin measurements DELPHI uses (Cheilopogon furcatus, Exocoetus volitans, Hirundichthys rondeleti), so sequence and morphometry are cross-species within Exocoetidae wherever used together.
The derived DELPHI record is an UNSIGNED nanopublication draft, pending a signing-key decision by the key holder: no human ORCID is attached and nothing has been published to a nanopub registry.
